extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies and plan developers preparing CAA section 111(d) state plans for fossil-fuel-fired steam generating EGUs, and EPA reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how states may invoke the Remaining Useful Life Of Facility (RULOF) provision in 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba when developing less-stringent standards of performance or longer compliance schedules for individual fossil-fuel-fired steam generating EGUs. Includes threshold demonstrations, evaluation metrics, evidence expectations, and how to calculate particularized standards/schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: State burden to document and justify standards of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: States always bear the responsibility of reasonably documenting and justifying the standards of performance in their plans; the EPA must be able to ascertain, based on the information and analysis included in the state plan submission, that the standard meets the statutory and regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must include sufficient information and analysis in plan submissions for EPA to determine compliance with statutory/regulatory requirements; this is a baseline requirement for any alternative standard or schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible use of RULOF
rubrics_metrics.description: RULOF may be used to particularize the compliance obligations for an affected EGU when a state demonstrates that it is unreasonable for that EGU to achieve the applicable degree of emission limitation or compliance schedule determined by the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invocation of RULOF does not modify subcategory membership or create a new subcategory; the particularized obligations must differ as little as possible from the presumptive standard and schedule for the EGU's subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold demonstration under 40 CFR 60.24a(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke RULOF a state must demonstrate that the facility cannot reasonably achieve the degree of emission limitation determined by EPA based on: (1) unreasonable cost from plant age/location/process design, (2) physical impossibility or technical infeasibility of installing necessary control equipment, or (3) other factors specific to the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state must show fundamental differences between facility-specific information and the information EPA considered in the emission guidelines that make achieving the guideline's degree of limitation or schedule unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline for RULOF comparisons (information EPA considered in BSER)
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline for considering RULOF is the information EPA considered in determining BSER for each subcategory, including: whether a system is adequately demonstrated, costs, non-air quality health and environmental impacts and energy requirements, and extent of emission reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States' demonstrations must be compared against this baseline; EPA's BSER analysis forms the starting point for evaluating fundamental differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on rate-based presumptive standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The emission guidelines provide presumptive standards of performance in the form of rate-based emission limitations; states should focus RULOF analyses on whether an affected EGU can reasonably achieve the applicable rate-based presumptive standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if other metrics or forms of standards exist, for these guidelines rate-based standards are the central comparison point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary cost evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA used $/ton CO2 reduced and $/MWh of electricity generated as cost evaluation metrics for determining BSER; states should evaluate costs using the same metrics to assess fundamental differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may consider additional cost metrics but must justify their relevance; using the same metrics facilitates objective and replicable comparisons to EPA's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other technical and non-air-impact metrics considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Under non-air quality health and environmental impacts and energy requirements, EPA considered parasitic load, boiler efficiency, non-GHG emissions, water use, CO2 capture plant siting, transport and geologic sequestration factors, and impacts on energy sector structure and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should use these metrics where relevant and may consider additional metrics not used by EPA if they are facility-specific and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cost as objective comparator
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, states should reflect source-specific considerations in terms of cost because cost is an objective and replicable metric for comparison to EPA's information and across EGUs and states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (e.g., pipeline length) are best expressed through cost impacts; cost comparisons aid consistency and defensibility of demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of remaining useful life via annualized costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Remaining useful life should be considered with regard to its impact on annualized costs; for purposes of determining annualized costs, EPA considers the amortization period to begin at the compliance date for the applicable subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state invoking RULOF on remaining useful life must demonstrate that annualized costs for a short-life unit are fundamentally different from the costs EPA found reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating fundamental cost differences
rubrics_metrics.description: A state must demonstrate that the costs of achieving the applicable degree of emission limitation for the particular affected EGU are fundamentally different from the cost values EPA considered (e.g., $71/ton CO2 reduced and/or $13/MWh in the co-firing example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs similar to EPA-determined reasonable costs (e.g., $18.50/MWh example) are not appropriate bases for RULOF; outlier costs (e.g., above 95th percentile fleetwide) could represent valid demonstrations but are not the only way to show a fundamental difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: No bright-line thresholds for reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's BSER cost analysis values are fleet averages and are not bright-line upper thresholds between reasonable and unreasonable costs; EPA is not setting generally applicable thresholds or presumptively approvable approaches in these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each RULOF demonstration must be evaluated on its particular facts and circumstances; illustrative examples in the preamble are not binding limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for 'other factors' specific to the facility
rubrics_metrics.description: States may invoke RULOF based on 'other factors specific to the facility' under 40 CFR 60.24a(e)(1)(iii), including categories of information or evaluation metrics EPA did not consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state must demonstrate that such other factor(s) make it unreasonable for the affected EGU to achieve the applicable degree of emission limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoking RULOF for a class of facilities (similar-situation requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoking RULOF for a class of facilities is only appropriate where all facilities in that class are similarly situated in all meaningful ways and share both the basis circumstance and all other characteristics relevant to determining reasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects this will rarely be satisfied for fossil-fuel-fired steam generating EGUs because units tend to differ in size, process, footprint, location, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirements for longer compliance schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a longer compliance schedule under RULOF, the state must substantiate with documentation (not speculative) that a particular EGU cannot reasonably comply by the guideline date and justify why certain implementation components will take longer than EPA considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong supporting evidence includes receipts, invoices, and actual site work demonstrating best efforts; the schedule must be no later than necessary and as close as reasonably possible to the guideline schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on use of RULOF for longer compliance (no speculative claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: States should not use RULOF to provide a longer compliance schedule unless there is a demonstrated, documented reason at the time of state plan submission that the source will not be able to achieve compliance by the guideline date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provides other flexibilities post-submission that states should consider; RULOF is for documented, non-speculative fundamental differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation requirement: standard/schedule no more lenient/longer than necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 40 CFR 60.24a(f), once threshold is met the state must determine a less stringent standard or longer schedule that is no less stringent or no longer than necessary to address the fundamental difference—i.e., as close to EPA's degree of limitation or schedule as reasonably possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final subpart Ba process requires evaluating, to the extent necessary, the systems of emission reduction EPA identified using the same factors and evaluation metrics EPA used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process when EGU is implementing BSER but cannot meet degree
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected EGU will be implementing the BSER but cannot meet the degree of emission limitation because of fundamental differences, the state may determine the degree the EGU can reasonably achieve and apply a less stringent standard based on that degree without needing to evaluate further systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if CCS capture achievable is 85% rather than EPA's 88.4%, the state may set a standard corresponding to 85% if no other system could achieve EPA's degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process when EGU is not implementing BSER and cannot meet degree under any system
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected EGU is not implementing BSER and cannot reasonably achieve the presumptive standard using any system of emission reduction, the state must follow the subpart Ba process to determine a standard or schedule no less stringent/longer than necessary (further procedural detail follows elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must evaluate systems EPA identified and use the same evaluation metrics and factors to the extent necessary; the less-stringent standard should remain as close as possible to the presumptive standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use EPA's evaluation metrics unless justified
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA believes states must evaluate costs using the same metrics EPA used ($/ton CO2 reduced and $/MWh generated) to determine fundamental differences, though states may include additional metrics if they justify relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should justify why any additional cost metrics are relevant to determining reasonableness for a particular affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and amortization timing detail
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining annualized costs for an affected EGU with a shorter remaining useful life, amortization is considered to begin at the compliance date for the applicable subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This detail affects comparisons of annualized cost burdens for RULOF demonstrations based on remaining useful life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of best efforts as support (but not exclusive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation that a source is making best efforts to achieve compliance (receipts, invoices, site work) is strong support for providing a longer compliance schedule but is not the only acceptable evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should show that need for additional time exists notwithstanding best efforts; other types of corroborating information may also be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No creation of new subcategories via RULOF
rubrics_metrics.description: Invocation of RULOF does not have the effect of modifying the subcategory structure or creating a new subcategory for a particular affected EGU; that EGU remains in the applicable subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any particularized standard or schedule must differ as little as possible from the subcategory presumptive standard and schedule.
